title: Objectwise cochain resolution and augmentation
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $C$ be a preadditive category with a zero object, and let $\iota:C\to A$ be fully faithful. Let $\Lambda=(F,\pi)$ be a left-resolution datum [lem-sfb-left-resolution-reduced-api] for $\iota$ (a functor $F:A\to C$ and a natural transformation $\pi:\iota F\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ with epimorphic components) whose functor $F$ preserves zero morphisms. Its cochain-complex resolution functor $R:A\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(C,\mathbb Z)$ is defined by iterating $\Lambda$ on kernels: $R(X)^q=0$ for $q>0$, $R(X)^0=F(X)$, $R(X)^{-1}=F(\ker\pi_X)$ with $d^{-1}$ the unique map satisfying $\iota(d^{-1})=\pi_{\ker\pi_X}$ followed by the inclusion $\ker\pi_X\to\iota F(X)$, and for $n\ge1$, $R(X)^{-n-1}=F(\ker\iota(d^{-n}))$ with $\iota(d^{-n-1})=\pi_{\ker\iota(d^{-n})}$ followed by the kernel inclusion; on morphisms $R$ acts through $F$ and the induced kernel maps. The augmentation is the cochain map $\iota R(X)\to X[0]$ (the complex with $X$ in degree $0$ and zero elsewhere) given by $\pi_X$ in degree $0$; it is natural in $X$. Every component of this map is a quasi-isomorphism, and every complex $R(X)$ is strictly supported in degrees $\le 0$; the same support assertion holds after applying $\iota$ termwise.

proof.text: The displayed functor F and natural transformation π with epimorphic components are exactly a Mathlib LeftResolution datum for the fully faithful functor ι; the zero-morphism-preservation assumption is retained. Thus the hypotheses of the left-resolution chain construction apply.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-left-resolution-chain-complex-functor]. It gives a functorial chain complex in C whose degree-zero term is F(X), degree-one term is F(ker π_X), and whose subsequent terms are F applied to the successive kernels of the ι-images of the preceding differentials; its maps are induced by F and kernel maps.

source.place: cochainComplexFunctor definition, lines 40–45, built from Mathlib chainComplexFunctor

proof.text: Extend this chain complex along ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat ($n\mapsto -n$). By [lem-sfb-left-resolution-complex-extension], the result $R(X)$ is a functorial $\mathbb Z$-indexed cochain complex whose term in degree $-n$ is canonically the chain degree-$n$ term, whose differential $R(X)^{-n-1}\to R(X)^{-n}$ is the chain differential $d_{n+1,n}$ under these identifications, and whose terms in positive degrees are zero; on maps it is the chain map in each degree $-n$. Substituting the terms and differentials of [lem-sfb-left-resolution-chain-complex-functor] gives exactly the displayed formulas: $R(X)^0=F(X)$, $R(X)^{-1}=F(\ker\pi_X)$ with $\iota(d^{-1})=\pi_{\ker\pi_X}$ followed by the kernel inclusion (map_chainComplex_d_1_0), and $R(X)^{-n-1}=F(\ker\iota(d^{-n}))$ with $\iota(d^{-n-1})$ the component of $\pi$ followed by the kernel inclusion (map_chainComplex_d), the induced maps being $F$ of the kernel maps.

The degree-zero map ι.map(F(X))→X is π_X. The differential into degree zero is, by map_chainComplex_d_1_0, the composite through π_{ker π_X} and the kernel inclusion, so π_X kills it by the kernel condition; hence these components define a cochain map to X[0]. Naturality follows from π.naturality and the functorial kernel maps in the chain-complex construction. This is precisely the augmentation cochain map and its naturality.

Since the target $X[0]$ is zero in every degree $\ne0$, quasi-isomorphism at $q\ne0$ means exactness of $\iota R(X)$ at $q$, and at $q=0$ it means: the short complex $\iota R(X)^{-1}\to\iota R(X)^0\xrightarrow{\pi_X}X$ is exact and $\pi_X$ is epic (the outgoing differential of $R(X)^0$ goes to the zero term $R(X)^1$). Degree $0$: by step 3 the first map is $\pi_{\ker\pi_X}$ followed by the kernel inclusion $\ker\pi_X\to\iota F(X)$; as $\pi_{\ker\pi_X}$ is epic its image is $\ker\pi_X$, so the short complex is exact, and $\pi_X$ is epic by hypothesis. Degree $-(n+1)$, $n\ge0$: by [lem-sfb-left-resolution-complex-extension] the degrees $-(n+2),-(n+1),-n$ all lie in the image of the embedding, so the short complex of $R(X)$ at $-(n+1)$ is isomorphic to that of the chain complex at $n+1$; applying $\iota$, exactness follows from [lem-sfb-left-resolution-chain-exactness]. Positive degrees: $R(X)^q=0$ for $q>0$ by [lem-sfb-left-resolution-complex-extension] and $\iota$ sends zero objects to zero objects (as in step 6), so $\iota R(X)$ is exact there. Hence the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism in every degree.

source.place: QuasiIsoAt and QuasiIso instances for cochainComplexπ, lines 137–168

proof.text: Finally, [lem-sfb-left-resolution-complex-extension] gives strict support in degrees $\le0$ for $R(X)$. Applying $\iota$ termwise preserves zero objects: if $Z$ is a zero object of $C$, then $\mathrm{Hom}_A(\iota Z,\iota Z)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_C(Z,Z)$ has one element because $\iota$ is fully faithful, so $\mathrm{id}_{\iota Z}=0$ and $\iota Z$ is a zero object of $A$. Hence $\iota R(X)$ is strictly supported in degrees $\le0$ as well.
